introduction:
A Registered Will is a pivotal legal instrument that ensures your assets and properties are distributed precisely according to your final wishes. By formally registering the Will under the Indian Registration Act, 1908, you provide it with an undisputed legal backing, significantly minimizing the chances of future familial disputes or fraudulent claims in West Bengal.

Registration ensures the document is safely preserved in the official government custody (Book No. 3), providing an authentic reference that cannot be easily tampered with, destroyed, or forged.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Is it Mandatory? No, registering a Will is optional in India, but highly recommended to prevent future disputes or challenges to its authenticity.
  • Jurisdiction: You must register the Will at the office of the Sub-Registrar (SRO) under whose jurisdiction the Testator (you) resides OR where a major part of the property is situated.
  • Stamp Duty: ₹0 (Zero). There is no Stamp Duty for registering a Will in West Bengal.
  • Fees:
    • Registration Fee: Nominal (approx. ₹50 – ₹100 depending on the district).
    • Standard User Charge: ₹300 (for Wills up to 17 pages). If it exceeds 17 pages, add ₹9 per extra page.
    • Court Fee: ₹10.
  • Witnesses: You need two (2) witnesses who must physically accompany you to the office.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: Carry the original and one set of self-attested photocopies of the following documents.
Core Documents & Proofs
  • Original Will: Printed on high-quality paper (legal size recommended). It does not need to be on Stamp Paper.
  • Identity Proof (Testator & 2 Witnesses): Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, PAN Card, or Passport.
  • Address Proof (Testator): Aadhaar Card, Passport, or Utility Bill (to prove you live in that SRO's jurisdiction).
  • Photographs: Two (2) passport-sized color photos each for the Testator and both Witnesses.
Medical & Portal Documents
  • Medical Certificate (Recommended): A "Mental Fitness Certificate" from a registered doctor (MBBS/MD) stating the Testator is of sound mind.
    • Note: While not strictly mandatory by law, Registrars in West Bengal often request this for senior citizens (above 60-65) to avoid future claims of "unsound mind."
  • Assessment Slip: The printout generated after filling the online form.
  • Payment Challan: Proof of payment (GRIPS challan) if paid online.
onlineApplication:
Online Application (e-Nathikaran Process)

West Bengal uses the e-Nathikaran system to initiate registration. This reduces time spent at the office.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1: Fill the e-Requisition Form
    • Visit the Directorate of Registration & Stamp Revenue website.
    • Look for "e-Requisition Form Filling" (often under the "e-Deed" or "Registration" section).
    • Fill in Details:
      • Applicant Details: Your name and phone number.
      • Transaction/Deed Type: Select "Will" from the drop-down list.
      • Party Details: Enter details of the Testator (person making the Will).
    • Submit: Once submitted, the system will generate a Query Number (keep this safe).
  2. Step 2: Generate Assessment Slip
    • On the same portal, use your Query Number to proceed to the "Assessment" section.
    • Since there is no market value assessment for a Will (unlike selling land), this step is quick.
    • The system will calculate the fees (Standard User Charge + Reg Fee).
    • Print the Assessment Slip. This document is mandatory for your office visit.
  3. Step 3: Pay Fees (GRIPS)
    • Go to the e-Payment section on the website.
    • Pay the calculated fees via the GRIPS (Government Receipt Portal System) using Net Banking/Debit Card.
    • Print the e-Challan/Receipt.
  4. Step 4: Book e-Appointment
    • Use the "e-Appointment" link on the homepage.
    • Enter your Query Number and select a convenient date and time to visit the Sub-Registrar's Office.
    • Print the Appointment Token.
offlineApplication:
Offline Application (The Physical Visit)

The "Offline" part is the actual execution at the Sub-Registrar's Office. You cannot do this by post or video call.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Arrive on Time: Reach the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) 15 minutes before your slot with all documents and your two witnesses.
  2. Verification: Present your Assessment Slip, Appointment Token, and Original Will at the verification counter. They will check the ID proofs of you and your witnesses.
  3. Biometrics:
    • You (Testator) and Witnesses will be called to the biometric desk.
    • Fingerprints and Photos will be captured digitally.
  4. Signing:
    • You will sign the Will in the presence of the Registrar.
    • Your witnesses will sign the Will in the presence of the Registrar and you.
    • The Registrar will digitally sign and endorse the document.
  5. Receipt: You will be given a Receipt (I-Ticket) containing the Deed Number. Do not lose this; you need it to collect the registered Will.
afterApplying:
After Applying — What Next?

Scanning & Collection

Your Will is scanned and uploaded to the central server for permanent record. The physical registration process usually takes about 1-2 hours on the day of the visit.

Delivery & Pickup

The final Registered Will (the physical document with the Registration Seal and page numbers) is usually delivered after 7 to 14 days (timelines vary by office). You (or a person authorized by you with the original receipt) must go back to the office to collect the original Registered Will.

Pro Tip (Commission Visit)

If the Testator is bedridden or hospitalized and cannot visit the office, you can apply for a "Commission" visit. For an extra fee, the Registrar will visit your home/hospital to complete the registration. This request must be made physically at the SRO beforehand with a medical certificate.
